intent.instructions: The message was typed by a school administrator in the chat of a Moroccan school management dashboard. It can be English, French, Spanish, Modern Standard Arabic or Moroccan Darija in Arabic or Latin script, or a mix. Which kind of request is it?

criteria.small_talk: Only a greeting, thanks, goodbye, or a question about what the assistant can do. No request for school data.
criteria.student_count: Asks only how many students are enrolled in the whole school this year: one number, not a list of students, with no filter by class, section, gender, status, date or anything else.
criteria.teacher_count: Asks only how many teachers the whole school has: one number, not a list or names of teachers, with no filter by subject, class or anything else.
criteria.student_and_teacher_count: Asks for both the total number of students and the total number of teachers, with no filter.
criteria.class_list: Asks to list or name the school's classes, with no filter and no question about their students, teachers or timetable.
criteria.attendance_today: Asks to see today's attendance for the whole school (who is present or absent today), with no class, student or other date, and not a number to compute.
criteria.upcoming_exams: Asks which exams are coming up or when the next exam is, for the whole school, with no class, subject or student filter.
criteria.write_request: Asks the assistant to create, add, record, mark, change, publish, send or delete something now, for example to record a student as absent or present today, including short Darija commands. Asking how to do it oneself is not this.
criteria.needs_llm: Anything else: a question with a filter or qualifier (a class, a student, a name, a gender, a past or other date, last year, a number to compute), a list of teachers or students, grades, fees, payments, timetables, how-to questions, a short follow-up that starts with "and" (et, y, و, w) or needs an earlier message, unclear requests and topics unrelated to the school.

is_write.instructions: The message was typed by a school administrator in the chat of a Moroccan school management dashboard. It can be English, French, Spanish, Modern Standard Arabic or Moroccan Darija in Arabic or Latin script, or a mix. Does it ask the assistant itself to create, add, record, mark, change, publish or delete data?

criteria.true: The user wants the assistant to make a change now.
criteria.false: The user only asks to see information, asks how to do something themselves, or makes small talk.

limitations: Latency is measured from this machine through OpenRouter, including TLS and network time.
Cases and intent wording were written by the same author; the dev/test split is not an independent evaluation.
Synthetic single-turn questions only: no follow-ups, conversation history or real school traffic.
Classification only: no reply, tool or template ran, so answer correctness is not measured.
